Subject: On-prem follow-up: offline ops, upgrade path & maintenance windows

Hi Anya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side and suggested next steps so we have alignment.

Recap of requirements you shared:
- Air-gapped/on-prem deployment; no outbound internet from inference hosts.
- Managed upgrades must happen during booked maintenance windows; Helios requires offline upgrade media and signatures.
- KMS/HSM integration required for keys (no cloud-managed KMS).
- Limited rack space and currently only 2x A100-class GPUs available; future add-ons may be quarterly.
- Strict logging/retention policy; audit logs must be exportable for SOC processes.

Questions we committed to answer:
1) How Redwood handles offline upgrades (image/patch delivery, signatures, rollback).
2) Hardware compatibility and a suggested min-spec for pilot vs production.
3) Maintenance runbook and patch cadence options (quarterly vs monthly).
4) What parts of the control plane remain in-customer (VPC) vs Redwood-managed.

Proposed next steps:
- I will share our private deployment upgrade playbook and a simple HW checklist (attaching).
- Sergio (SE) will propose an upgrade/rollback runbook and staging plan.
- If acceptable, propose a 2-week pilot window in early November for an offline install test.

Attachments I will send in follow-up: helios_hw_spec.xlsx, redwood_private_upgrade-path.pdf, and a one-page MOP.

If that sounds right, can you confirm the preferred maintenance windows (days/times) and whether Helios requires signed binaries for every patch?

Best,

Thanks Rishi — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Yes, air-gapped only. Any upgrade media must be delivered via signed artifact on removable media (USB/tape) — we cannot pull from the internet.
- Our datacenter team limits hot-swaps; for GPU adds we need a scheduled two-day window and on-site vendor support.
- For high-risk patches we require a cryptographic signature + a rollback image that has been validated in staging.
- Audit logs retention is 7 years, but we only need token-level request logs forwarded weekly to our SIEM connector.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can produce signed binaries and provide an offline verification checksum process? Also would like to see a simple checklist we can give to our datacenter ops team (power, network isolation, USB signing process).

Cc'ing our integrator (deploy@onsite-integrations.com) who will help coordinate the physical delivery.

Hi Anya / Rishi — we can support airgap deliveries and staging. A few practical notes from our installs team: 
- We recommend shipping signed artifacts on encrypted USB drives with tamper-evident seals.
- We will bring a validated rollback image for each patch (kept on a separate sealed device).
- For environments that disallow USB we can deliver sealed NVMe with signed images and hand it to on-site engineers.
- We need a minimum 4-hour maintenance window per node for non-disruptive patching; full rollback testing requires a staging slot.

We will review Redwood's MOP and map it to our delivery SOP. Sending our install checklist in a follow-up attachment.

— Onsite Integrations, Delivery Team

Subject: Re: On-prem follow-up: offline ops, upgrade path & maintenance windows

Anya — looping in a couple folks and attaching a more detailed upgrade/runbook draft. Key points up front: 

1) Offline upgrade model we support:
   - Signed release bundles generated by Redwood CI; each bundle has a SHA256 checksum and a vendor signature (we can provide a signing key certificate for Helios to validate).
   - Delivery options: encrypted USB, sealed NVMe, or SD cards for air-gapped transfer.
   - Each upgrade includes an auto-verified pre-check that runs against hardware inventory; if pre-check fails, the node is left unchanged.

2) Rollback and staging:
   - We provide signed rollback images. Rollback is orchestrated locally via a maintenance agent that runs entirely offline.
   - Recommended flow: staging node -> validate image -> snapshot KV stores -> run upgrade -> smoke tests -> promote.

3) HW compatibility and pilot sizing:
   - Minimum pilot: 2x A100 (40GB) + 512GB RAM + 2x 10GbE NICs.
   - Production guidance for throughput targets attached in helios_hw_spec.xlsx.

4) Maintenance cadence options:
   - Quarterly security patches (low risk) or monthly critical fixes. We suggest quarterly for your environment but can support both.

Attachments: redwood_private_upgrade-path.pdf, helios_hw_spec.xlsx, mop_helios_onprem.docx

Please review the attached runbook; nothing in the flow requires network egress from inference hosts. We do use a customer-managed control-plane in the VPC for orchestration metadata, which can be confined to Helios' network per your policy.

If that aligns, propose the pilot install week of Nov 9 — Onsite Integrations, can you confirm availability?

Thanks,
